metaDescription: Instinct's public API surface: read-only accessors, Fabric events, the veterancy-rate provider hook, and the convention tags third-party mods extend with plain data.
title: Developers
lede: One stable package — com.rfizzle.instinct.api — per the Concord API standard: read-only accessors, provider/callback registration as the only mutation, isModLoaded-guarded consumption. Everything here is specced and lands with implementation.

rows: pets-set membership after full resolution (config → tags → heuristic)
mounts-set membership after full resolution — the horse family by default; a mount gets self-preservation and downed/revival only
provider hook — multiplies live veterancy accrual; error-isolated, clamped to sane values
after grade resolution at breeding — parents, child, final grade
when a pet or mount enters the downed state — animal and damage source
on every path back up — animal, reviving player, item used. Kennel-post recovery passes a null reviver and an empty stack

sections.title: Convention tags and data — integrate with zero code

headers: What one data file gets you
rows: Entity-type tags — opt your mod's species in or out of the three coverage sets explicitly
Entity-type tag — small pets a rescuer can pick up and carry while downed
Entity-type tag — species a stationed pet turns off the pasture (foxes and wild wolves by default)
Item tag — your feed items become trough-accepted; animals eat them by their own breeding-food rules
Item tag — your item revives downed pets (ships with golden apples and the Vet Kit)
Item tag — non-edible items the generic drop-bonus fallback may duplicate
One file per species: primary/secondary products (and cooked variants) for grade drop bonuses; unknown ids skip harmlessly, so rows for absent mods are safe to ship

blocks.html: Item ids for sibling integrations: instinct:command_whistle, instinct:vet_kit, instinct:pedigree_treat, instinct:keepsake_collar; the blocks are instinct:feeding_trough and instinct:kennel_post. Full contracts in design/SPEC.md; suite conventions in the Concord API standard.
